glossary.definition: (A)(1) "Public authority" means the state, a state institution of higher education as defined in section 3345.011 of the Revised Code, a county, township, municipal corporation, school district, or other political subdivision, or any public agency, authority, board, commission, instrumentality, or special purpose district of the state or of a political subdivision.
glossary.scope: As used in sections 153.65 to 153.73 of the Revised Code:

glossary.definition: (2) "Public authority" does not include the director of transportation when exercising the director's authority to prepare plans for, acquire rights-of-way for, construct, or maintain roads, highways, or bridges.
glossary.scope: As used in sections 153.65 to 153.73 of the Revised Code:

glossary.definition: (B) "Professional design firm" means any person legally engaged in rendering professional design services.
glossary.scope: As used in sections 153.65 to 153.73 of the Revised Code:

glossary.definition: (C) "Professional design services" means services within the scope of practice of an architect or landscape architect registered under Chapter 4703. of the Revised Code or a professional engineer or surveyor registered under Chapter 4733. of the Revised Code.
glossary.scope: As used in sections 153.65 to 153.73 of the Revised Code:
As used in sections 153.65 to 153.73 of the Revised Code:

glossary.definition: (E) "Design-build contract" means a contract between a public authority and another person that obligates the person to provide design-build services.
glossary.scope: As used in sections 153.65 to 153.73 of the Revised Code:

glossary.definition: (F) "Design-build firm" means a person capable of providing design-build services.
glossary.scope: As used in sections 153.65 to 153.73 of the Revised Code:

glossary.definition: (G) "Design-build services" means services that form an integrated delivery system for which a person is responsible to a public authority for both the design and construction, demolition, alteration, repair, or reconstruction of a public improvement.
glossary.scope: As used in sections 153.65 to 153.73 of the Revised Code:

glossary.definition: (H) "Architect or engineer of record" means the architect or engineer that serves as the final signatory on the plans and specifications for the design-build project.
glossary.scope: As used in sections 153.65 to 153.73 of the Revised Code:

glossary.definition: (I) "Criteria architect or engineer" means the architect or engineer retained by a public authority to prepare conceptual plans and specifications, to assist the public authority in connection with the establishment of the design criteria for a design-build project, and, if requested by the public authority, to serve as the representative of the public authority and provide, during the design-build project, other design and construction administration services on behalf of the public authority, including but not limited to, confirming that the design prepared by the design-build firm reflects the original design intent established in the design criteria package.
glossary.scope: As used in sections 153.65 to 153.73 of the Revised Code:

glossary.definition: (J) "Open book pricing method" means a method in which a design-build firm provides the public authority, at the public authority's request, all books, records, documents, contracts, subcontracts, purchase orders, and other data in its possession pertaining to the bidding, pricing, or performance of a contract for design-build services awarded to the design-build firm.
